questions.question: What is sent to the server on submit?
options: The name of each control along with its value.
questions.explanation: The name of each form control is sent to the server along with the value the user enters or selects.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: The name of each form control is sent to the server along with the value the user enters or selects.

questions.question: When does the browser send that data?
options: When the user presses a button to submit the form.
questions.explanation: A user fills in a form and then presses a button to submit the information to the server.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: A user fills in a form and then presses a button to submit the information to the server.

questions.question: Which control is for a single line of text such as a name?
questions.explanation: Text input (single-line) is used for a single line of text such as email addresses and names.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: Used for a single line of text such as email addresses and names.

questions.question: Which control is for longer messages?
questions.explanation: Text area (multi-line) is for longer areas of text, such as messages and comments.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: For longer areas of text, such as messages and comments.

questions.question: Radio buttons are for when the user must?
options: Select and unselect one or more options.
Select one of a number of options.
questions.explanation: Radio buttons: one of a number of options. Checkboxes: one or more.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: For use when a user must select one of a number of options.

questions.question: Checkboxes are for when the user can?
options: Pick only one option in the group.
Select and unselect one or more options.
questions.explanation: Checkboxes: select and unselect one or more options.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: When a user can select and unselect one or more options.

questions.question: Why does each control need a <label>?
options: It makes the form accessible to vision-impaired users.
Labels are how CSS colors the input.
questions.explanation: Each form control should have its own label element as this makes the form accessible to vision-impaired users.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: each form control should have its own <label> element as this makes the form accessible to vision-impaired users.

questions.question: Which label wrapping pattern does Duckett show first?
options: <label> wrapping the description and the input.

A

before the input with no for/id.
questions.explanation: The label element can wrap around both the text description and the form input.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: Wrap around both the text description and the form input

questions.question: How does <label for="female"> connect to an input?
options: The input's name must be female.
The input's id must be female.
The input's type must be female.
The form's action must be female.
questions.explanation: for points at the control's id, as in the gender radios.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett

questions.question: What must radios in one group share?
questions.explanation: The gender radios share name="gender" and differ by id and value. Shared name makes them one choice.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett

questions.code:
<input id="female" type="radio" name="gender" value="f">
<input id="male" type="radio" name="gender" value="m">

questions.question: Which drop-down matches 'pick one of a number of options from a list'?
questions.explanation: Drop-down boxes: pick one of a number of options from a list. That is select, not a made-up dropdown tag.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: When a user must pick one of a number of options from a list.

questions.question: A password field differs from text how?
questions.explanation: Password input is like a single line text box but it masks the characters entered.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: Like a single line text box but it masks the characters entered.

questions.question: What does a submit button do?
options: Submit data from the form to another web page.
questions.explanation: Submit buttons submit data from your form to another web page.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: To submit data from your form to another web page.

questions.question: Why include name on an input?
options: Browsers refuse to paint unnamed inputs.
The server receives name=value. No name, nothing sent for that control.
name is an alias for id.
name is a CSS selector only.
questions.explanation: The name of each control is sent with the value. Skip name and that field is missing on the server.

reference.excerpt: The name of each form control is sent to the server along with the value
